scope: HOSTED round for barcode (Extension 8) and for the two servers whose value only exists when they talk to each other, kanban and time-tracker, through the URL-token endpoints https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/<server>/t/<token> as a claude.ai user arrives. Eighteen prompts, six per lane: barcode from Part 2 of docs/BARCODE_AUDIT.md (QR SVG, SEPA QR from an amount and a reference with the business profile set on /mcp/invoice first, EAN-13 from 12 digits, WiFi, the monthly count, a PNG that hits the Pro gate); kanban with time-tracker registered so the cross-endpoint handoff is live; time-tracker alone, which had never been scored on its own. Free tier, one fresh anonymous token, one seed (invoice business_set by curl).
method: One anonymous token minted with GET https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect (anon_99d439c70625548432cd7f127d9b7793, 7916-byte page) and reused for every lane. Registered PER LANE only, because the free tier is 600 calls per hour per token and a CLI session re-handshakes every registered endpoint on every turn (D-R53): barcode alone, kanban+time-tracker, time-tracker alone. Client: claude CLI 2.1.260, --model sonnet, --mcp-config with type http and the /t/<token> URL, --strict-mcp-config, no headers anywhere, per-tool allowlist of 40 mcp__<server>__<tool> entries built from a live tools/list (barcode 10, kanban 16, time-tracker 14), --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 20, one --session-id then five --resume per lane. Per r11 D-R57 every lane ran in an EMPTY working directory with the CLI own filesystem tools disallowed (Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, NotebookEdit); nothing shelled out. The kanban lane and the time-tracker lane write the same store and so ran sequentially; barcode ran alongside. Tool-call counts exclude the client ToolSearch schema lookups. Machine day 2026-09-04, a Friday, on a UTC+07 host, which is what makes k1 and the timesheet clock interesting.
rubric: 3 = correct, right numbers, no clarification. 2 = correct but needed a second turn, a workaround, or left the user a gap to close. 1 = partially wrong, or asked for something the tool could infer. 0 = failed.

scenarios.prompt: Plan my week for Nova: API design (3h, due Wednesday), docs (2h, Friday), client call prep (1h, Tuesday).
scenarios.note: Board created, three tasks stored. Today is itself a Friday and the D-K6 rule resolves a bare weekday to the nearest day on or after today, so Docs landed on 2026-09-04 while Tuesday and Wednesday rolled to next week. The model caught it and spent a fourth call, task_update {due: 2026-09-11}. Identical to r11; the rule is documented and left alone.
One board: five columns, 3 tasks in backlog, 6h estimate, nothing overdue. The per-task table the model printed came from the k1 transcript, not from board, and every row matched task_list by curl.

W36, Nova: 1 completed, estimate 3h against actual 1h 30m, '1h 30m under' relayed, and it said unprompted that the two tasks due 09-08 and 09-11 fall in W37 and are outside these numbers.

defects.title: qr_payment_sepa required the IBAN and name the shared business profile already held, so the model asked the user and drew nothing
defects.fix: servers/barcode/src/index.ts: iban and name optional, resolved through readSharedProfile() the way invoice_payment_qr already did, with the same business_set refusal when neither exists and an explicit argument still winning; the response says where the beneficiary came from. Two tests in servers/barcode/test/smoke.test.mjs. Verified live: 'Pay Nova Studio at PL61109010140000071219812874, EUR 1230.00. Beneficiary taken from the shared business profile.'

defects.title: the hosted $19 PNG gate never said a hosted PNG barcode has no human-readable digits under the bars
defects.fix: remote/build-vendor.mjs patchBarcodeIndex names it in the refusal a free caller reads and in the success line a Pro caller gets; keyed off the barcode_ feature name so the qr tools, which have no human-readable line, are untouched. Verified live.

defects.title: timer_stop's rate note told the caller to call entry_update, a tool that does not exist
defects.fix: now entry_edit {id, rate, currency}. servers/time-tracker/test/round13.test.mjs is the general form: it parses the registered tool names out of src/ and fails on any 'name {' citation in a string literal that is not one of them, with non-vacuity asserted in both directions.

defects.title: entry_list printed the day in the profile home zone and the clock in the host process zone: 09:00 Warsaw came back as 2026-09-03 07:00
defects.fix: hhmm() in servers/time-tracker/src/day.ts formats in the same home zone dayKey uses. Tested across a UTC-day boundary. Verified live: the same row now reads 2026-09-03 09:00.

defects.fix: direction: when the whole requested window falls outside the free window, say nothing in it was read, the way calendar.conflicts and currency.rate_history shorten and name what they covered (docs/GUARDRAILS_RESULT.md)

insight: One species of defect, three times over: the server knows something the caller is never told. It knew the beneficiary and asked for it anyway, knew a hosted PNG has no digits and sold it silently, knew the entry's timezone and printed another one. Only the first cost a point, because the model papered over the others - it paraphrased the nonexistent tool name and repeated the hours rather than the clock. A description-only fix is also what let D-R64 survive from BARCODE_AUDIT to this round: the model never read the description that was fixed, because it never picked that tool.
